raw_response:
I farm a small 6 mu wheat-maize rotation in Quzhou, and with only two people in the household, I would keep the plan steady, practical, and not too input-heavy. I would plant all 6 mu to winter wheat first and then all 6 mu to summer maize on the same land, because that is the normal local double-cropping system and it fits my irrigation conditions. For wheat, I would use improved seed rather than going cheap on old seed, because I want stable emergence and lodging resistance. I would keep fertilizer around a medium level instead of chasing the highest possible yield: for irrigated winter wheat in southern Hebei, the Ministry of Agriculture’s guidance for 500-600 kg/mu fields is roughly in the range of moderate base fertilizer plus spring topdressing, which works out to about 14 kg N, 6-7 kg P2O5, and around 5 kg K2O per mu in practical use ([MOA 2021](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202109/t20210916_6376525.htm)). I would irrigate wheat three times if water is available: once around green-up, once at jointing, and once around grain filling, because wheat in Quzhou depends heavily on timely water. I would keep pesticide to two passes unless pressure gets bad: one weed control pass and one combined disease/insect pass near the key spring stage.

For summer maize, I would switch the same 6 mu over immediately after wheat harvest and use hybrid seed, because in Hebei maize production guidance emphasizes good hybrid seed, timely sowing after wheat, and strong stand establishment ([Hebei 2025 maize guidance](https://nyncj.sjz.gov.cn/columns/86f1c43c-897d-4b4f-b83d-ee6e7fe11683/202506/24/2b46ecd8-58b6-4109-909d-f3d5c5efb908.html)). I would not overwork the soil after wheat harvest; I would use no-tillage or the lightest possible disturbance so I can sow fast and save labor. I would keep maize fertilizer moderate too, because in wheat-maize systems the phosphorus effect partly carries over from the wheat season, and Hebei guidance still centers maize around timely nitrogen, especially at the big flare stage ([MOA wheat-maize rotation note](https://www.moa.gov.cn/ztzl/qnszcgdfs/201005/t20100526_1493334.htm), [Hebei 2025 maize guidance](https://www.cfsn.cn/news/detail/616/301792.html)). So I would use about 15 kg N, 5 kg P, and 4 kg K per mu, with the main nitrogen timed for the large bell stage. I would plan two irrigations for maize: one if emergence is dry, and one around tasseling/silking to avoid drought at the critical stage, because Hebei guidance specifically warns about “卡脖旱” around heading and silking. I would also keep pesticide to two passes, mainly one for weeds early and one around the big flare stage for borers and leaf diseases. I would aim for solid, realistic yields rather than maximum-input yields.
